answers.d01: 似然和后验概率回答两个方向相反的问题。似然问：假设成立时，看到眼前这批数据的可能性多大？后验问：看到这批数据后，假设本身有多大可能成立？用硬币说：假设「这枚硬币公平」，掷10次得9次正面，似然是P(9正|公平)=C(10,9)×0.5¹⁰≈1%——固定假设，评估数据。而「这批数据之后，硬币仍公平的概率」是后验，方向是固定数据、评估假设，两者数值通常不同。关键差别：似然不是「假设为真的概率」。比较「公平硬币」和「90%偏正面的硬币」时，似然只用来比大小：后者算出约39%，远高于1%，说明数据更支持这个假设；但各假设的似然加起来不必等于1。要变成后验，得用贝叶斯公式乘上先验——你看到数据前对每个假设的相信程度。同一批数据，先验不同，后验就不同；而似然只由数据和假设决定。
answers.d02: The average tells you where a list's center sits; variance measures how spread out the values are around it. Take 2, 4, 6: mean 4, deviations −2, 0, +2. You cannot average the deviations — they always sum to zero, which would make every dataset look perfectly concentrated. Squaring prevents that cancellation: 4, 0, 4, averaged to 8/3 ≈ 2.67. Variance is the average squared distance from the mean. Squaring is a choice, not a law — absolute values would also stop cancellation — but squaring punishes large deviations much harder: one value 10 off contributes 100, while ten values 1 off contribute 10 in total. So variance is outlier-sensitive, which is either the point or the flaw depending on your question. Side effect: units get squared (kg²), so we usually report the square root, the standard deviation. Note how it scales: doubling every value's distance from the mean makes variance four times larger.
answers.d03: 正反馈的核心是：输出反过来加强输入，变化自己给自己添柴。话筒靠近音箱，扬声器放出的声音被话筒拾回，再放大、再播出，一圈圈绕下去就变成刺耳的啸叫——每绕一圈都更响，这就是「放大」的来源。注意「正」说的是方向：反馈与原变化同向叫正反馈，反向抑制变化的叫负反馈；它本身不是评价。评价好坏要看被放大的是什么：学习越学越有信心、越有信心越愿意学，是良性的正反馈；银行谣言引发挤兑，挤兑造成的损失又坐实谣言，是恶性的。两者机制完全相同，只是结果一个我们想要、一个不想要。放大也不会无限持续：音箱音量受电源和喇叭极限限制，挤兑受存款总量限制。判断时先找回路——结果是否回到起点加强了自己——再看能量从哪来、上限在哪里。
answers.d04: 机会成本是你选了某个用法后，放弃的那个「最好的其他选择」的价值。周六下午空闲三小时，你可以加班挣200元、看一场你愿意花80元买票的电影、或者补觉。假如你选了补觉，机会成本不是200加80，而是加班的200元——只有被放弃选项里最好的那一条算数，因为如果补觉取消，你会转去加班。两点容易错：一是以为免费就没成本，「免费」往往只指不用掏钱；二是把所有备选加总，实际被牺牲的只是一项。价值也不一定是钱：看电影的机会成本可以是200元工资，加班的机会成本也可以是你更需要的休息。决策的用处在于让隐性代价显形：问一句「这个下午我放弃了什么最好的可能」，如果答案让你犹豫，说明当前选择未必最优。
answers.d05: 体检阳性就一定得病了吗？贝叶斯公式回答的正是这个问题：阳性里有多少是真病人。设想一万人体检，患病率1%，即100名病人；试剂灵敏度99%，查出99人；但健康人也有5%被误判，9900人中约495人呈阳性。于是594份阳性里真病人只占99，约17%。公式写出来就是：P(患病|阳性) = P(阳性|患病)×P(患病) ÷ P(阳性)。分母594是全部阳性人数，分子99是其中真病人的部分。容易混淆的两个99%：一个回答「病人里多少呈阳性」，另一个（17%）回答「阳性里多少是病人」，方向相反。把患病率改成10%，其余不变：真阳性990人、假阳性仍约450人，阳性后患病概率跳到约69%——基础比例越高，同样的检测越可信。垃圾邮件过滤同理：判断一封含「中奖」的邮件是不是垃圾，也要乘上垃圾邮件本身的基础比例。
answers.d06: A cache keeps a fast local copy of slow data — the server stores a product's price so it need not query the database on every page view. The catch: copy and original are separate storages, and the copy never learns on its own when the original changed. Cache invalidation is the decision about when a cached copy stops being trustworthy and must be dropped or refreshed. Example: the page is cached for 5 minutes, the team cuts the price, and for up to 5 minutes customers see the old figure — possibly checking out at a stale amount. Two common policies: a TTL simply expires copies after N seconds — simple, but freshness is only guaranteed up to N; or the write path actively deletes the cache entry when the price changes, so the next read refetches — fresher, but writes now touch two systems. It is called a hard problem because at scale copies live in many places; updating one leaves the others serving stale data.
answers.d07: 冰淇淋销量高的月份，溺水人数也多。两者相关——一起变大变小——但买冰淇淋不会让人溺水，把冰淇淋店全关掉，溺水照旧。背后有个共同原因：天气热。天热让更多人买冰淇淋，也让更多人下水，两个数字于是同涨同跌，这叫混杂变量。判断标准一句话：相关是「一起变」，因果是「动这一个，另一个跟着变」。把人随机分成强制买冰淇淋和不买的两组，若溺水率没差别，因果就不成立；随机分组之所以可靠，是因为天气这类混杂因素被随机摊平了。相关不等于因果还有别的来路：可能是方向反了（不是失业导致生病，而是生病导致失业），也可能是样本被挑过（去医院的病人死亡率高，不说明医院害人）。看到相关先问三句：有没有共同原因？方向会不会反？样本是不是被挑出来的？
answers.d08: Compound growth is growth on growth: each period's gain is computed on the running total, not the original amount. $1,000 at 10% a year becomes $1,100, then $1,210, then $1,331 — after t years, 1,000 × 1.1^t. Everyone's multiplier 1.1^t is the same; only the starting principal scales it. That is why the start matters: $100 at the same rate becomes $259 in ten years while $1,000 becomes $2,594 — the tenfold gap never closes by itself, because a fixed rate multiplies whatever you have. Starting earlier works through the exponent instead: $1,000 invested at 25 rather than 35 gives, at 65, about $45,300 versus $17,400 — ten extra years nearly tripled it. Time cuts both ways: over a few years compounding barely bites and small rate differences hardly matter; over forty years, 7% versus 5% more than doubles the gap in outcome. The judgment to carry: check the horizon before weighing any rate.
answers.v01: 过拟合是「把旧题背得滚瓜烂熟，新题一变就不会」。一个学生把每道练习题连答案带印刷错误全背下来，练习卷满分；考试换了数字，他全盘崩溃。学习模型同样如此：给它十个人的身高和体重，它能画出一条扭曲的曲线，精确穿过每一个点——包括那几个测量误差造成的偏离点。训练数据上误差为零，但那些「怪点」不是规律，记住它们反而干扰对新数据的预测。判断不看过拟合的模型在旧数据上的成绩，只看没见过的数据：旧数据满分、新数据糟糕，就是过拟合。条件变化很直接：数据越少、模型越自由，越容易过拟合；把十个点增加到一千个，怪点被大量正常点稀释，模型只能学出真正的趋势。它付出的代价是记住噪声，换来的好处是训练分数好看——理解过拟合，就是看清这笔交换。
answers.v02: A search returns 10 documents; 6 are truly relevant, and the corpus actually holds 20 relevant ones. Precision asks: of what came back, how much was right? 6/10 = 60% — it measures how much junk you wade through. Recall asks: of everything relevant out there, how much was found? 6/20 = 30% — it measures what you missed. The two trade off. Loosen the matching to return 40 documents: maybe 18 of the 20 get caught, recall jumps to 90%, but precision sinks to 45% since 22 irrelevant ones tag along. Tighten it and the reverse happens. Which to prioritize depends on the cost of each mistake: legal discovery fears missing documents, so it favors recall; a web engine has ten slots where a wrong hit is glaring, so precision at the top matters more. Beware single numbers: returning one lucky result gives 100% precision while telling you nothing about recall.
answers.v03: 常见误解是「长颈鹿拼命伸脖子，脖子就变长传给后代」。自然选择不是这样：先有随机变异，再有环境筛选。一群鹿里天生就有脖子略长略短的差别，这不是谁努力练出来的；旱年矮处树叶吃光时，脖子长的吃得更多、活得更久、留下的后代更多。注意变的是下一代种群里的比例——长脖子基因的频率上升——而不是某只鹿的身体被拉长。缺一不可的三件事：变异存在、变异可遗传、不同变异留下后代的数量不同。筛选也不预知方向：环境说哪个「有利」，哪个才被留下；环境一变结论就翻转。细菌就是现成例子：抗生素使用之前，群体里已随机存在少数耐药变异；用药后普通菌死光，耐药菌占了整个种群，并不是细菌「练出」了抗药。检验一个说法是否搞错，就问一句：变异在选择之前就已经有了，还是被「用出来」的？
answers.v04: An operation is idempotent when doing it once and doing it five times end in the same state. Distributed systems force this on you because networks lose responses: your service asks to charge $50, the payment provider completes it, but the reply is lost in a timeout — so you retry, and without protection the customer is charged twice. Retries are routine, so side effects must survive them. Compare: status = shipped is idempotent, since rerunning writes the same value; balance += 10 is not, since each run adds. The standard tool is an idempotency key: the client attaches a unique ID to the request, the server records processed IDs, and a repeat with the same ID returns the stored result instead of executing again. One clarification: idempotency concerns the final state, not wasted work — a repeated GET may recompute, but nothing changes. Design every write so a duplicate cannot distort it, because duplicates will arrive.
answers.v05: 信息熵衡量面对一个随机结果时你有多难猜。定义是每个结果的概率乘以它的意外程度（−log p），再加总：H = −Σ p·log p。稀有结果出现很意外（−log p 大）但很少出现，常见结果不意外但占大头，熵就是平均下来的意外量。为什么均匀概率最不确定？对比两枚硬币：正反各半时，你无法偏向任何一边，只能纯碰运气，熵为1比特；另一枚99%正面，闭眼猜「正面」就有99%把握，熵只有约0.08比特。可利用的把握越小，熵越大；各结果概率相等时毫无信息可用，不确定性达到上限。这也是判断依据：拿到任何概率分布，先看它离均匀有多远，越远越可预测。条件一变结论跟着变：同一颗骰子被做了手脚后，各面概率不再相等，熵随之下降。
answers.v06: Deadlock: two parties each hold a resource and wait for the other's, so neither can ever proceed. Concrete case: transaction A locks row 1, then asks for row 2; transaction B locks row 2, then asks for row 1. A cannot finish without row 2, so it never releases row 1; B is symmetric. Both wait forever — that is the deadlock. It requires all four conditions at once: resources are exclusive (one holder at a time), holders keep what they have while waiting, nothing can be forcibly taken away (no preemption), and the waits form a circle (A→B→A). Remove any one and deadlock becomes impossible, which is why the standard fix is lock ordering: every transaction locks rows in ascending ID order. Then B must ask for row 1 first, fail, and wait — the circle never forms. Now change the case so A needs only row 1: the problem vanishes, showing the circular wait was the load-bearing condition.
answers.v07: 公共物品是这种东西：没法把没付钱的人排除在外（非排他），而且多一人享用也不减少别人的份（非竞争）。小区装楼道声控灯，装好后每层住户都照到，你无法只让出钱的人享受光明；国防、干净的空气、防洪堤都是如此。这带来搭便车问题：既然不掏钱也能用，每个人都盼着别人出钱、自己白享结果。十户人都这么想，灯就装不成——尽管每户愿意出50元、总共500元远超300元成本，对大家明确有利的事却办不成。对照着看：面包不是公共物品，不付钱就不给你，一人吃了别人吃不到，所以市场供得起；公共物品收费困难，市场供给往往不足，这就是为什么这类东西常由税收出钱、由集体决定。判断一件东西是不是公共物品，就问那两条：能不能排除不付钱的人？一人多用一分会不会挤占别人？
answers.v08: Little's law says L = λW: the average number of items in a system (L) equals the arrival rate (λ) times the average time each item spends there (W). It is bookkeeping, not a claim about any special queue: if 10 customers per minute enter a café and each stays 5 minutes, a typical moment finds 10 × 5 = 50 customers inside. Its power lies in what it does not assume — arrivals can be random, service irregular, one server or many; as long as the system is stable, the identity holds. So a service handling 1,000 requests per second while holding 100 requests in memory averages 0.1 s latency (100 / 1000). It also tells you where to act: lower latency means fewer items in the system or a slower arrival rate, since the three are bound together. And it lets you compute whichever variable is hardest to measure directly from the other two.
